SECTION I
Purpose, Scope, Basis, and Definitions
Purpose:
Article 1- The purpose of this Directive is to regulate the working principles regarding the
execution of Psychological Counseling and Guidance Services provided by Gebze Technical
University Directorate of Health, Culture and Sports.
Scope:
Article 2- This directive covers the use of the Psychological Counseling and Guidance Service,
the operation of the service, the duties of the counselor, and all the authorities and
responsibilities related to the service.
Basis:
Article 3 - This Directive has been prepared in accordance with the provisions of the
"Implementing Regulation for Medico-Social, Health, Culture and Sports Affairs Directorate
at Higher Education Institutions" dated 03/02/1984 and numbered 18301.
Definitions:
Article 4-
(1) Psychological Counseling: It is a development process in which people receive help for
determining their goals, making decisions, solving existing problems and similar issues from
educated counselors who are impartial, respectful of personal rights and attach importance to
trust and confidentiality for personal, social, educational, and professional matters.
(2) Guidance: It is a systematic and professional process of helping the client understand,
recognize the opportunities around, and realize himself/herself by making the right decisions.
In this Directive, the following terms have the following definitions:
a) Directorate: Directorate of Health, Culture and Sports
b) Client: Every individual who will receive Psychological Counseling and Guidance Services
c) Counselor: Psychologist who provides Psychological Counseling and Guidance Services
d) GTU: Gebze Technical University
e) Psychologist: Professional who graduated from the Psychology Department of the relevant
faculties of universities
f) Rector: Rector of Gebze Technical University
g) Session: Jointly planned meetings of the Client and the Counselor

SECTION II
Procedures for Benefiting From, Operation and Duties of Psychological Counseling and
Guidance Services
Procedures for Benefiting from the Services:
Article 5 – The following may benefit from Psychological Counseling and Guidance Services:
a) GTU staff and first degree relatives of the staff
b) GTU retired staff and their first degree relatives
c) Those with an active student enrollment at GTU
How the Services Operate:
Article 6-
a) Client Registration and A dmission: Psychological Counseling and Guidance service is
provided via an online appointment system. The client who wishes to make an appointment
creates his/her appointment through the GTU Appointment Tracking System on web. When the
appointment time arrives, the client is admitted into the session by showing his/her university
ID if he/she is a student or a staff member or by showing his/her ID card and the staff member’s
university ID if he/she is a relative of a university staff member.
b) Appointment System: If the appointment is delayed more than 15 minutes, a new online
appointment must be made. Clients who cannot attend their appoi ntment must cancel their
appointment via the Appointment Tracking System.
c) Session Procedure: Clients are asked to fill out the Staff and Student Application and
Consent Form. In the Consent section of the form, the person is informed about the operation
of the session, its duration, continuity, confidentiality, psychiatric support, harmful behavio r,
etc., and his/her signature is obtained. The first session is called pre-interview and covers topics
such as determining the person's problems, obtaining information about the person, and getting
to know him/her. Session duration is 50 minutes for individual sessions, 90 minutes for family
sessions, group sessions, and couple sessions. Sessions are planned once a week or once every
15 days with the approval of the person.
d) Application of Test s: The psychologist may apply Psychological Test s and Inventories
when deemed necessary while conducting the sessions. As a result of the test s, information is
obtained about the behavioral patterns, emotional state , and psychological problems that the
client may not be able to express.
e) Psychiatric Support: The psychologist does not have the authority to write reports or
prescribe medication as a mental health specialist. If the psychologist finds it necessary while

f) Termination of Sessions: After continuing the sessions with the client for a certain period

Duties:
Article 7- Psychological Counseling and Guidance Services consist of the following:
a) To provide newly-enrolled students with introductory and informative information about the
university, its rules and the immediate environment, and to ensure that the student gets used to
the environment and the university;
b) To deliver seminars to students, academic and administrative staff, to organize events on
certain days and weeks, to carry out necessary work within the scope of social projects on issues
that concern the society;
c) To identify the client's problems and cooperate with relevant institutions to solve them;
d) To help students who wish to change their department to recognize their interests and abilities
and make appropriate choices;
e) To inform students about the profession they will have in the future and job opportunities in
the surrounding area. To help graduates find employment by collaborating with private and
public institutions and to monitor job-placed graduates within their means;
f) To provide psychological counseling for students with emotional problems, academic and
administrative staff, individually or in groups, according to their wishes and needs. To help the
client make im portant decisions, know himself/herself better, and establish more effective
relationships with the people around himself/herself;
g) To ensure that preliminary interviews are conducted by the authorities in cases referred as
related to students, academic and administrative personnel and that psychological tests are
applied to them when necessary. To refer the client to the relevant service division according
to the results of the evaluation.
SECTION III
Miscellaneous Provisions
Miscellaneous Provisions:
Article 8- The provisions of the relevant legislation apply to all matters not covered in this
directive.

Enforcement:
Article 9-
a) This directive enters into force from the date it is accepted by the Senate of Gebze Technical
University.
b) With the adoption of this Directive by the Senate, the "Gebze Technical University Directive
for Psychological C ounseling and Guidance Services ", which is currently in force , will be
abolished.
Execution:
Article 10- This directive is executed by the Rector of Gebze Technical University.
